scope: All48 saved source-addressed editions. Different numerical forms are not claimed as48 independent mathematical meanings. No author solver or test answer imported.

universalProofs.coprimeDefinition: Coprime means the complete common positive-divisor set is exactly{1}; new counterexamples refute all other universal choices.
universalProofs.consecutive: For arbitrary n, symbolic coefficient subtraction (n+1)-n=1. Any common positive divisor divides1 and must equal1. This is general, not inferred from finite samples.
universalProofs.difference: Any common divisor of n and n+D divides their linear difference D. Conversely every divisor d ofD occurs by n=d, so the possible gcd set is exactly the complete positive-divisor set ofD.
universalProofs.guaranteed: g=gcd(A,B) divides every pair of respective multiples. Taking the numbers A,B themselves shows every universal divisor must divide g; hence the greatest is exactly g.
universalProofs.scaling: Bezout: ua+vb=g. If d divides ka andkb, then d divides u(ka)+v(kb)=kg. Conversely kg divides both ka,kb. Thus gcd(ka,kb)=kg for every positive k, independently of the author prime-factor proof.
